title: A draining tank cannot gain energy, including after it empties
rationale: With the inflow off, dH/dt = -grad_H^T R grad_H <= 0, at EVERY step and ANY step size -- which is what distinguishes a structure-preserving integrator from a merely accurate one. The horizon deliberately runs past the emptying time (10.6 s) so that the energy trace has a flat tail: while the level is still falling steeply a small energy leak hides inside the true decay, and the fixture only becomes sensitive once the energy has flattened. The tail also exercises the trap that H = (1/2) rho g A h^2 is EVEN in h, so a step overshooting below empty reads back as INCREASED energy; a model that does not clamp the head at zero passes or fails depending on where its final step lands -- that is, on the grid rather than on the physics. The exact drain law is checked separately by water_tank_drain_law; this fixture is about passivity alone.

parameters._units: A, a in m^2; g in m/s^2; c_d dimensionless; rho in kg/m^3

checks.closed_form: dH/dt <= 0 for u = 0, at every step

H(60 s) = 0: the tank empties at 2A sqrt(h0)/(c_d a sqrt(2g)) = 10.6 s and an empty tank stores no energy. A frozen model that never drains fails here, so 'energy never increased' cannot be satisfied by doing nothing.
